note: printf TRUNCATES a commit message at a bad format character and git commits the partial text with exit 0 — a silently half-landed message that looks fine in the summary line. Hit it on a message containing an apostrophe-escape; the last three paragraphs vanished. The repo rule (PROC-commit-message-via-file) says write the message to a file, and the safe way to write that file is a QUOTED heredoc (<<EOF with the delimiter in single quotes), never printf. Recover with git commit --amend -F.
